newsitem.title: ITALY: China says it has no problems with food.
newsitem.headline: China says it has no problems with food.

text.p: China dismissed fears on Friday that agricultural problems could mean it would have trouble feeding people in the world's most populous nation.
Chinese Premier Li Peng told the World Food Summit in Rome that his country could use increased grain yields and exploit more land to maintain its self-sufficiency.
"It is entirely possible for China to maintain its food needs in the future," he said.
"People can rest assured that, in the coming years, not only will the Chinese people maintain food sufficiency, they will also make contributions to food security in the world."
China has more than one billion people, around one-fifth of the world's population, but only seven percent of the planet's arable land.

The five-day U.N.-sponsored summit has been discussing ways to end hunger and a leading food expert warned earlier this week that China would find it increasingly difficult to grow the grain it needs to sustain its booming economy.

Lester Brown, president of the Worldwatch Institute, a private Washington-based monitor of food supplies, told a news conference that China was losing croplands at a record rate, turning it from a net grain exporter two years ago to the second biggest importer behind Japan in 1995.
In his speech on Friday, Li insisted China was still a net grain exporter.

Jacques Diouf, director general of the Rome-based Food and Agricultural Organisation (FAO), told Chinese television in an interview this week that Beijing was working hard to meet the growing demand for food.
